items.question: Why do you want to join Anthropic?
lookFor: Specific reasons tied to the mission and to something you've read (RSP, Core Views, an engineering post).
Bridge from your industrial customer background to bringing Claude safely to industrial customers.
Evidence you've built with Claude yourself.
No generic enthusiasm or 'performing alignment'.
followUps: Why this role and not engineering?
What would you want to change at Anthropic?

items.question: What are your views on Anthropic's research papers? Pick one you've read.
lookFor: Names a real paper/post (e.g. Building effective agents, Contextual Retrieval, Demystifying evals for AI agents, Core Views) and summarises it accurately.
Gives an opinion: what you applied, agreed with, or questioned.
Connects it to customer work (e.g. workflow vs agent choice, eval harnesses).
followUps: What would you tell a customer from that paper?
What's missing from it?

items.question: Would you be fine if the stock went to zero?
lookFor: Honest answer about motivation: mission and work over equity upside.
Shows you understand the mission could require hard choices (e.g. pausing development).
Doesn't sound rehearsed; acknowledges personal financial reality honestly.
followUps: What would make you stay if compensation were lower than elsewhere?
What does 'put the mission first' mean to you in practice?

items.question: In 150 words, write your answer to 'Why Anthropic?' for the application.
lookFor: Your own first draft (Claude may refine it, per Anthropic's candidate guidance).
2-3 specific reasons, one of them about safe deployment in industries like manufacturing.
One concrete proof point from your platform work.
followUps: Which sentence would a recruiter remember?
What did you cut?

items.question: Give me your 90-second pitch for this Industries role.
lookFor: Three beats: 10+ years technical customer-facing in industrial equipment (CH/CN/US) -> solo-built an AI platform in production -> wants to help industrial customers adopt Claude.
One crisp result from each phase.
Ends with why Anthropic specifically.
followUps: Which industry would you be most useful in?
What's your weakest area for this role?

items.question: Tell me about a technical presentation you gave to a mixed audience of engineers and executives.
lookFor: How you structured for both audiences (business outcome first, details in backup).
A moment you adjusted live based on the room.
Outcome: decision made, deal progressed.
followUps: What question surprised you?
What would you do differently?

items.question: Your live demo breaks in front of a customer. What do you do? Has it happened to you?
lookFor: Stays calm, explains what happened honestly, falls back (recording, screenshots, step-through).
Turns it into a discussion of failure modes and how production would handle them.
Follows up with a working version and a short write-up.
followUps: How do you prepare demos to reduce risk?
When would you not demo live?

items.question: Describe how you'd run a half-day discovery workshop with a manufacturer's operations, IT and quality teams.
lookFor: Agenda with clear goals and roles; pre-work (process maps, sample documents).
Use-case brainstorm -> prioritisation by value, feasibility, risk -> 1-2 candidates.
Gets IT/security constraints and eval ownership on the table early.
Ends with a written recap, owners and next steps.
followUps: How do you handle one loud stakeholder dominating?
What do you do if the top use case is not a good fit for an LLM?

items.question: Your internal champion at a customer leaves halfway through a pilot. What do you do?
lookFor: Multi-threading: relationships beyond one person.
Re-establishes the business case and success metric with the new owner.
Example from your sales/service experience.
followUps: How do you spot this risk early?
What if the new person wants to cancel?

items.question: Tell me about a complex sale with many stakeholders (technical, procurement, executives). How did you move it forward?
lookFor: Mapped stakeholders and their criteria (e.g. equipment buyer, plant engineer, finance).
Tailored technical proof to each (trials, acceptance tests, references).
Concrete outcome and timeline; what you'd do differently.
followUps: Who almost blocked it?
How did you work with your sales counterpart?

items.question: Your account executive promised a customer something Claude can't reliably do. How do you handle it?
lookFor: Raises it privately with the AE first; aligns on the message.
Resets expectations with the customer honestly and proposes an achievable alternative with an eval.
Protects long-term trust over short-term deal pressure.
followUps: What if the AE disagrees?
Has something like this happened in your past roles?

items.question: Give an example of turning repeated customer feedback into a product or process change.
lookFor: Noticed a pattern across customers, not one complaint.
Quantified it and brought it to the right internal team.
Result, and how you closed the loop with customers.
followUps: How would you do this at Anthropic?
What if the product team disagreed?

items.question: Tell me about a time you told a customer 'no' or 'not yet' for safety or quality reasons.
lookFor: Real situation with stakes (equipment limits, an unready AI workflow).
How you explained the risk and offered a path (smaller scope, test first).
Outcome and what it did to trust.
Connects to RSP/Core Views thinking without forcing it.
followUps: Did it cost you the deal?
Where is the line between caution and being unhelpful?

items.question: Describe an ambiguous ethical tradeoff you faced at work. How did you decide?
lookFor: Genuinely ambiguous (no obvious right answer).
How you reasoned, whom you consulted, what you decided.
Honest reflection on whether it was right.
followUps: What would you do now?
How would you handle a similar tradeoff for an AI deployment?

items.question: Tell me about a mistake you made, how you discovered it and how you fixed it.
lookFor: Ownership without excuses.
Immediate containment and transparent communication.
Systemic fix (check, guardrail, process) and what you learned.
followUps: Who did you tell first?
Could it happen again?

items.question: A customer wants an agent with unrestricted write access to their production systems. What do you do?
lookFor: Understands the business goal first.
Proposes least-privilege tools, approval gates for irreversible actions, audit logs, staged rollout.
Explains risk in the customer's terms; knows when to escalate internally.
followUps: What if they insist?
Which actions could safely run without approval?

items.question: What's the biggest risk of deploying LLMs in regulated industries like pharma or energy, and how would you help a customer manage it?
lookFor: Specific risk (e.g. confident wrong answers on safety-critical procedures, data leakage, unaccountable decisions).
Concrete mitigations: evals on real cases, citations, human approval, audit trail, scoped pilots.
Balanced: doesn't claim risks are solved; also doesn't discourage valuable use.
followUps: How would you explain residual risk to a regulator?
When would you advise not to use an LLM?
